modules.behavior: UART 8N1 receiver with 16x oversampling, a two-flop input synchronizer, a three-sample majority vote, start-bit validation and framing-error detection. Public parameter OVERSAMPLE_DIV=2 is the number of clk cycles per oversample tick; supported domain integer 1..64. Preserve the actual OVERSAMPLE_DIV-dependent timing, not only the default. Let D = OVERSAMPLE_DIV and B = 16*D (clk cycles per bit). Synchronizer: registers sync1 <= rx and sync2 <= sync1 at every rising edge, both reset to 1; the line sample L used at edge i is sync2 before edge i, i.e. rx as it was before edge i-2. States IDLE, BUSY and WAIT_IDLE; reset state IDLE. In IDLE the first edge with L = 0 is the detection edge e0 and enters BUSY. In BUSY, at edge e0 + m (m >= 1) the frame offset is m, the bit index is b = m div B (0 start bit, 1..8 data bits LSB first, 9 stop bit) and the phase is p = m mod B. At p = 7D, p = 8D and p = 9D the receiver takes L as three votes for bit b; at the p = 9D edge the bit value is the majority of the three votes and is decided at that edge. L at every other BUSY edge is ignored, so the line may carry anything there. Start bit (b = 0): majority 1 is a false start: return to IDLE at that edge with no output (the next edge may detect again); majority 0 continues the frame. Data bit b in 1..8 becomes received bit b-1 (LSB first). Stop bit (b = 9, decided at edge e0 + 153D): return to IDLE at that edge; majority 1 registers rx_data = the 8 received bits and pulses rx_strobe = 1 for exactly one cycle; majority 0 pulses frame_err = 1 for exactly one cycle, leaves rx_data unchanged and enters WAIT_IDLE. In WAIT_IDLE the first edge with L = 1 returns to IDLE without detecting, so a line held low produces exactly one framing error and a new frame can be detected at the following edge. Outputs are registers that change only at rising edges: rx_strobe and frame_err are 0 except for their one-cycle pulses, rx_data holds the last good byte (0 after reset). Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns to IDLE and sets sync1 = sync2 = 1, rx_data = 0, rx_strobe = 0 and frame_err = 0; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge given the rx value present before that edge; keep sync1, sync2, the state, the frame offset, the votes and the received bits in state and return rx_data, rx_strobe and frame_err as registered by that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled. The examples hold rx constant from the reset state: with rx = 0 the detection edge is edge 3 (L lags rx by two edges), so with D = 2 the all-zero frame's stop bit is decided at edge 3 + 153*2 = 309, where frame_err pulses; frame_err is 0 again after edge 310 and the still-low line never re-triggers.
modules.name: uart_rx_core

modules.behavior: Synchronous first-word-fall-through byte FIFO with registered occupancy and an overflow pulse. Public parameter ADDR_BITS=2 sets the capacity DEPTH = 2^ADDR_BITS entries; supported domain integer 1..4; preserve the parameter. count is the number of stored bytes, 0..DEPTH. out_valid = (count != 0); out_data = the oldest stored byte when out_valid = 1 and 0 when out_valid = 0. Both depend only on registered state: there is no combinational path from wr_en, wr_data, out_ready or rst to any output. At each rising edge with rst low, using the inputs present before the edge: pop = out_ready && count != 0 removes the head byte; push = wr_en && (count < DEPTH || pop) stores wr_data behind all remaining bytes, so a full FIFO accepts a write at an edge where it also pops; a push and a pop at the same edge keep order and leave count unchanged. A byte written into an empty FIFO is visible after that edge, never in the same cycle (no bypass). overflow is a register: after an edge where wr_en = 1 and push = 0 (the byte is dropped) it is 1 for one cycle, otherwise 0. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge empties the FIFO and clears overflow; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the queue in state and return out_data, out_valid and overflow as they are after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state (empty) and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: rx_fifo

modules.behavior: Two 4-bit saturating event counters. At each rising edge with rst low: if ferr_in = 1 and ferr_count < 15 then ferr_count increments by 1; if ovf_in = 1 and ovf_count < 15 then ovf_count increments by 1; a counter at 15 stays 15 (saturates, never wraps). Inputs are sampled only at rising edges and both outputs are registers. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge clears both counters; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep both counts in state and return ferr_count and ovf_count as registered by that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: rx_err_count

When known=false, absence of a top annotation is not a failed or unverifiable criterion. Unannotated numeric latency is UNKNOWN, not zero. Preserve the source's exact observable cycles and registered behavior. Annotation presence or absence alone is not independent proof of behavioral correctness; use the fixed source contract, all defined typed latency/minimum transfer age and deterministic verification, without inventing a numeric requirement.

implementation.meaning: Chip-top implementation: the top is the whole FPGA design. Every port bit gets an I/O buffer on a package pin, and data ports have zero input and output delay to clk, so the routed WNS and WHS include pad delay. Utilization includes the I/O buffers.

metric_provenance: Structured metrics are parsed from retained reports; routed utilization/timing reports take precedence when present. The manifest identifies complete files by hash. Header excerpts are bounded previews, not complete reports or an independent metric source.
objective_policy: First establish timing feasibility. A verified timing-feasible candidate may replace a known timing-infeasible previous best even with higher area or power; classify this as timing_recovery, not objective savings. While the previous best is timing-infeasible, a verified still-infeasible candidate with strictly better setup WNS and hold not worse beyond a small tolerance may replace it as timing_progress, which is not closure; a feasible candidate always outranks it. Once both are timing-feasible, require strict improvement of the chosen objective; for maximize_freq that is register-to-register setup slack (reg2reg_wns_ns) when both designs report it, otherwise full setup WNS for both, while feasibility stays on full WNS and WHS. minimize_luts compares (lut_used, ff_used) and minimize_ffs compares (ff_used, lut_used) lexicographically: an equal primary metric with a strictly lower secondary is an objective improvement, a higher primary never is, and a secondary missing from either design gives no tie-break. Unknown or contradictory incumbent timing evidence cannot establish recovery. A completed experiment may find no improvement. Do not invent mandatory savings, slack margins, tool versions, timing corners, new tests, thresholds, code-style quotas or external environment requirements.
